runs.text: Directions: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.

w• 审题思路 • 作文要求以“机器人在未来校园中的应用”为话题展开论述。首段点明科技发展背景，引出“机器人将融入校园生活，重塑日常体验”的核心观点。主体段围绕机器人在校园中的应用场景进行分层论述。一是强调机器人在学习与科研场景的辅助作用，有助于提升学术效率；二是阐述机器人在校园日常事务中的应用，如物资配送、校园卫生等，为师生提供便利；三是说明机器人在校园安全管理中的功能，如夜间巡逻、隐患预警等，筑牢校园安全防线。最后一段总结全文，重申机器人对校园的积极影响。 ////

参考范文 I With the rapid development of technology, robots have gradually been applied in various industries and fields. Consequently, robots, for my part, will also be introduced into campus life in the future, reshaping students' daily experiences. 2 To begin with, robots will become powerful assistants in learning and research. In laboratories, robots are able to finish repetitive operations and record experimental data accurately, which improves the overall efficiency of experiments. In addition, robots can handle various campus affairs. For instance, intelligent delivery robots can transport packages or meals to dormitories, while robotic cleaners keep the campus tidy. Last but not least, robots can create a safer environment. Security robots can patrol at night, detect smoke or abnormal sounds, and then send alerts to the control center immediately. To sum up, robots will bring great convenience and efficiency to future campuses. 3 There is no doubt that they will make our campus life more colorful.

runs.text: News Report One A 104-year-old woman is selling the house she has lived in since she was two years old. [1] Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street. She is now putting it on the market, having lived in it through the Second World War and the invention of television. Her family bought the house for 200 pounds in 1921. And it is now priced at some 170,000 pounds. According to the Bank of England's inflation calculator, 200 pounds in 1921 would be worth 7, 750 pounds today. According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882 and originally featured a well for the entire road. Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same. [2] Mrs Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health. 1. What does the news report say about NancyGitford？关于南希•吉福德，新闻报道中提到了什么？ A）她出生于第一次世界大战结束数月之后。 B）她一生都住在这栋房子里。 解析 答案为 A）。句［1］提到，南希•吉福德出生于第一次世界大战结束数月之后。A）项对应录音内容， 故为答案。其中 was born months after the end of 为录音原词复现，World War I 对应录音中的the First World Waro 干扰项排除 录音开头提到南希•吉福德正在出售她从两岁起就一直居住的房子，而非一生都住在这栋房子里，故排除B）项；录音只提到南希•吉福德在这栋房子里经历了第二次世界大战（having lived in it through the Second World War），但并未提及她在第二次世界大战期间遭受了很多苦难，C）项属于无中生有，故排除；D）项中的102年是南希•吉福德在房子里居住的时长，且录音开头点明她是104岁（A 104-year-old woman），D）项与录音内容不符，故排除。 2. Why is Mrs Gifford selling the house？吉福德夫人为何要出售这栋房子？ A）她被房产经纪人劝说卖房。 B）她因为健康问题而急需用钱。 解析 答案为D）。句［2］提到，吉福德夫人打算卖掉房子，搬到附近格拉斯顿伯里的一家养老院，原因是她的身体状况不佳。D）项是对录音中 moving to a nursing home的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音未提及房产经纪人劝她卖房，故排除 A）项；录音只提到健康问题是她搬家的原因，但未提及她因为健康问题而急需用钱，B）项属于过度解读，故排除；格拉斯顿伯里是养老院所在地，她是搬去这里，而非离开，C）项与录音内容相悖，故排除。 News Report Two The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder. [3] The man, 47, wrote the word HELP in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue. The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs. To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth. He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking. He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success. Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror. He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. [4] He was found in good health but had lost weight.
C）她在第二次世界大战期间遭受了很多苦难。 D）她是居住在萨默塞特村的一位102岁老人。
C）她将离开格拉斯顿伯里村。 D） 她将要搬去养老院。

3. What does the news report say was key to the man's rescue? 新闻报道称，什么对该男子的获救起到了关键作用？ A）海军及时抵达。 B）他丰富的航海经验。 解析 答案为C）。句［3］提到，这名47岁男子在船上写下了英文单词“HBLP”，这成为他救的关键。 C）项是对录音中 wrote the word HELP in English on the boat 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除 海军是最终实施救援的一方，但录音并未说海军及时抵达是男子获救的关键，故排除A）项；录音未提及男子有丰富的航海经验，故排除B）项；利用镜子发出信号是男子中途尝试的求救手段，但这只是辅助行为，不是他获救的关键，故排除D）项。 4. What do we learn about the man when he was rescued？我们可以了解到这名男子获救时的什么信息？ A）他完全失去了意识。 B）他身体状况良好。 解析 答案为B）。句［4］提到，他被发现时健康状况良好，但体重减轻了。B）项是对录音中 was found in good health的同义转述，故力答案。 干扰项排除录音未提及他失去意识以及悲痛消沉，A）项和C）项属于无中生有，故均排除；录音提到男子尝试多种求救方法：在船上写下英文单词 HELP（wrote the word “HELP" in English on the boat）、用布收集雨水 （collected rainwater with a cloth）、生火发出求救信号（light a fire to send a distress signal）以及用镜子发出信号 （signaled with a mirror），这一系列自救行为表明他并非陷入绝望，故排除D）项。 News Report Three [5] The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment. The specific schools will be announced in the coming days, a district spokesperson said. The school board approved criteria to close schools with fewer than 215 students, as well as schools with fewer than 275 students and a projected decline in enrollment. [6] In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3, 000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said. 3, 000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you're receiving per-pupil funding, that's about 36 million dollars, district spokesperson Scott Bribble said. "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work, [7] but in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said. The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollments. 5. What do we learn about the elementary and middle schools to be closed in Denver? 关于在丹佛将要关闭的小学和中学，我们了解到了什么？ A）它们为提供社会服务所做的努力被忽视了。 B）它们遭到了丹佛校董事会的批评。 解析 答案为D）。句［5］提到，丹佛公立学校董事会计划关闭几所小学和中学，以弥补因人学人数下降而导致的预算减少。由此可知，丹佛将要关闭的小学和中学的入学人数已出现下降趋势。D）项是对录音中 declining enrollment的同义转述，故答案。 干扰项排除 录音提到的是预算减少意味着无法再提供同样的心理健康支持、社交和情感服务（the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services),* 提供社会服务所做的务力被忽视了，故排除A）项；B）项和C）项在录音中均未提及，故排除。
C）写在船上的单词“HELP”。 D）他利用镜子发出信号。
C）他悲痛消沉，无法振作。 D） 他彻底陷入绝望。
C）它们采取了多种措施以争取更多的经费。 D）它们的入学人数已出现明显的下降趋势。

6. What does the Denver district expect to do in the next three years？丹佛校区预计在未来三年内会怎样？ A）通过针对经费缩减而关停学校的标准。 B） 小学和中学的入学人数将減少3000人。 解析 答案为B）。句［6］提到，该校区表示，在未来三年内，预计小学和中学的入学人数将减少3000人。 B）项是对录音中 enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students 的原词复现，故为答案。 干扰项排除 录音中提到学校董事会通过了关闭学校的标准（The school board approved criteria to close schools），这是已经发生了的事情，而非未来三年内会发生，A）项时间范围错误，故排除；录音中明确提到具体关停学校名单会在未来几天公布（The specific schools will be announced in the coming days），而不是未来三年才决定，故排除C）项；录音中提到学区是按人头拨款，但录音并未提及要修改这一政策，故排除D）项。 7. Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson? 根据校区发言人的说法，丹佛的一些学校为什么要关闭？ A）为了让校区保持竞争力。 B）为了避免对当地经济造成负面影响。 解析 答案为C）。录音开头提到了丹佛校区计划关闭一些小学和中学，其后丹佛校区发言人在句［7］明确提到，为了让校区不陷入债务，这是必须采取的一步。必须采取的一步（a step that needs to be taken）即关闭一些学校。由此可知，C）项是对录音中 in order for the district to stay out of debt 的同义转述，故为答案。 干扰项排除“让校区保持竞争力”和“当地经济”在录音中均未提及，故排除A）项和B）项；录音表明生源减少会导致拨款变少，“获取预期的经费”与录音逻辑相反，故排除D）项。
C）确定要关停哪些小学和中学。 D）基于合理依据修改按人头拨款政策。

Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.

C) The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk-but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes-developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.

D) "I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry  professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."

These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.

F) Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying  illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
G) Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.

People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance.

Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed. It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and selfdoubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings. Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well. The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender. A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language. One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other. Music is tied to specific perceptual (di fut), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics  (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos). There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

那些系统性低估自己和自身表现的人，患上了所谓的冒名顶替综合征。［46］他们认为任何成功都归因于外界因素，或仅仅是运气和偶然。这类人终日惶恐，担心自己的“骗局”会被揭穿。 人们偶尔质疑自身能力是很正常的。［47］适度的自我反思与自我怀疑能让人避免冲动行事。然而，有一部分人即便表现优异，却始终深陷强烈的自我怀疑之中。他们不认为成功源自自身本领或勤奋，反而将成就归结于外部因素，比如运气和偶然，或是觉得别人严重高估了自己的表现。而失败时，他们又总会将问题归咎于自身的不足。 哈雷-维滕贝格马丁•路德大学的心理学家首次在真实生活条件下研究了这一现象。研究共有76 名受试者参与，他们完成了一系列智力测试，且无论实际表现如何，所有人都收到了积极的反馈。随后研究人员询问他们， 认为自己取得不错成绩的原因是什么。 该研究得出两点结论：首先，受试者自述的冒名顶替综合征程度，与实际测量的智力水平或表现并无关联。 ［48］其次，研究支持了这样一种假设，即有这类心理倾向的人，会贬低他们经过客观测评过的表现，把好成绩归功于运气和偶然等外部因素，而非自身能力。这些结果也和他们的年龄和性别毫无关系。 ［49］长期低估自己能力的人，往往还会心存顾虑：害怕这种所谓的智力欺诈迟早会被戳穿，并为此付出代价。 冒名顶替综合征由美国心理学家宝琳•克兰斯与苏珊娜•艾姆斯于 1978年首次提出。两位学者发现，有特别多的事业有成的女性都认为自己算不上聪慧。冒名顶替综合征不被定义为一种精神疾病。［50］然而，患有此征的人表现出更高的抑郁易感性。 /////////

• 全文翻译• 音乐是一种通用语言。在每一种文化、每一个国家，你都能发现音乐的身影。［51］它在全球范围内都有着至关重要的作用，并且有能力让人们在平和融洽中凝聚在一起。在音乐相关的种种体验里，我最喜爱的一种，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐人组成团队同台 绎。［52］当每种文化都为这个团队带来自身独有的特色时，一种全新的声音便由此产生。这能创造出非同凡响的效果。人们可以借助这门通用语言彼此进行交流。 不同文化之间存在一个共通的音乐纽带，那就是五声音阶。令人惊讶的是，诸多文化在音乐创作中都会使用这一体系。五声音阶由五个音构成，“penta-”意为数字五，“tonic”则指音调、乐音。［53］这种音阶在各地的音乐中都能见到，包括美洲原住民、非洲人以及亚洲人的音乐。在流行乐、蓝调、爵士乐和摇滚乐里也能找到它的踪迹。借助这种五音音阶，全球的音乐人拥有了交流的媒介，他们可以借此建立联结、沟通、表演，最终彼此理解。 音乐与人类特定的感知、思维和情感能力息息相关，包含语言能力（所有社会都会为歌曲配上歌词）、动作控制能力（所有地区的人们都会随音乐起舞）、声音辨析能力（所有音乐体系都拥有独特的音高与音色）以及审美能力（它们的曲调与节奏在重复与错落无序之间达到平衡）。

目前已知的社会，无一不存在音乐。虽然每种文化都拥有独具特色的风格与表现形式，但你会发现，世界各地音乐存在的目的却高度相似。［54］音乐本质上用于抒发或改变情绪：它能让人心情愉悦、心生伤感、怒火中烧或是情绪亢奋。音乐常常用于各类仪式，出现在宗教活动、典礼与庆典之中。音乐也可以单纯用作消遣：带来愉悦、欢乐与趣味。［55］无论你以何种方式使音乐，几乎可以肯定，其他所有文化也都以同样的方式运用音乐。 正是这一点将我们所有人紧密相连。我们都由衷热爱音乐，而音乐也拥有团结所有人的力量。 •
